title: The Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions
main_claim: For every ε>0, ||K_δ f||_{L^3(S^2)} ≤ C_ε δ^{-ε} ||f||_{L^3(R^3)}. The proof assumes the critical exponent h(p,0) is positive for every p near 2 and derives a contradiction. Lemma 2.x gives a differentiability point with h>0 and h_z>0. From there the paper builds equality configurations, a canonical profile F=β(κ-τ)_+ and stationary packets. Entropy rates for the four matrix coordinates have to meet a demand Q ≥ τ+B_*, and planar projection/pinning constraints rule this out. Separately, Prop 'maximal reduction' turns h(p,0)=0 into the L^3 maximal bound with loss δ^{-(p-2)/3-κ}.
coverage: Partial coverage of a 7.7k-line paper. Checked line by line: (1) Sec 2 (10-critical.tex): the indexed model; validity of A=d-1 via Cauchy-Schwarz and pair counting by slope; the monotonicity h(p,z+s) ≤ h(p,z)+s; the passage from BV to total differentiability and the argument 0<h(p,0) ≤ ∫h_z; existence of hybrid and exact equalities; regularization lemma (ii); cost lemma. (2) Sec 3 (05-inputs.tex): the weighted convex-clustering extension of GWZ Thm 1.1 (random sampling, box net, Chernoff bounds); conversion from plank bounds to convex clustering, using the ellipsoid volume = (2/3)·height·max-slice identity; the Ren–Wang exponent translation k·δ^{-min(t,(s+t)/2,1)}, consistent with min(s+t,(3s+t)/2,s+1); weighted Guth endpoint multilinear Kakeya and the cube corollary. (3) Sec 70 closure: all five cases in the case table, recomputed by hand. These are the pointwise bound M-τg/2 ≤ 2ℓb_+ and the gaps T_*-U_1, U_2, U_3, U_4, and K_0, including the coefficient bounds from η ≤ min(1/32,(p_min-2)/16) and the v_* ≤ β/2 trace argument. Also checked: the definitions of the case quantities match Sec 50 (k=(0,τ,ℓ,1), y_1=j_Y, u_1=j_U) and the constraints in Prop projection-rates. (4) Full maximal reduction: the discrete estimate via h(p,0)=0 with Δ_0 ≤ C from slope separation; tube/cylinder enlargement constant 64; the distribution bound; summing over level sets with Hölder. (5) Sec 60: the frame-change formula and width ratios, which use τ+ℓ=1. (6) Sec 30: the packet-mass exponent identity, verified with sympy; the canonical-profile first-passage limit; the uniform prefix slack k²m/n ≥ N^{h+(p-2)α}. (7) Sec 50: entropy demand ∂_cH ≥ s_0ℓ+wg-M; central value ∂_cH(c,0)=dw-B_*-τ+s_0ℓ; offset bound H(c,a) ≥ H(c,0)+da; stripe demand Q ≥ τ+B_*. Not line-checked: Sec 20 (local geometry, positive deficit, angle packing, prefix extension, flat delay), Sec 40 (angular Frostman beyond its setup, conditional-X), the proof of Prop projection-rates and the pinning lemma (Sec 60/65), and Lemma gap-density / remove-label. Also not independently checked: whether the cited GWZ Thm 1.1 and Ren–Wang Thm 4.1 statements match the papers verbatim.
sibling_notes: Sibling rank28 (4D Kakeya full Hausdorff dimension) depends on this paper's Lemma 2.3 (weighted planks). That is the 'Weighted set estimate in a line chart' lemma in 05-inputs.tex, and I checked it: the plank bound gives weighted convex clustering with constant O(A) via an enclosing ellipsoid and translated max-slice rectangle, and the GWZ set theorem is applied after random sampling at a log loss. I found no problem there.
